clue.text: Exchange bit of grass for flick-knife

parts.note: to exchange one thing for another is to switch them
a single leaf of grass is a blade

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a stalk of grass for a flick-knife, a strange trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A flick-knife is a knife whose spring-loaded blade shoots out at the press of a button; the American name is a synonym.

clue.text: Group studying ruined remains

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Students are examining archaeological ruins and remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class of students meeting for discussion of a topic.

clue.text: Cream trailer containing gold

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant that trails along walls
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A cream-coloured trailer carrying a load of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Trailer suggests a vehicle; it is a plant that trails.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a pale off-white shade, much like cream as a colour.

clue.text: Unexpected over large part of church

parts.note: chance as an adjective means accidental, as in a chance meeting
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Something unexpected happens over a big area of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area round the altar for clergy and choir, a section of the building.

clue.text: Brownie stands to embrace soldier back inside

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first word holds another
inside confirms the soldier goes within the other word

parts.note: to stand something is to bear it, so bears

indicators.note: back means the word for soldier is turned round

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A Brownie Guide stands to hug a soldier home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns GI into IG. Big-Ears is the brownie (a small elf-like sprite) who is the friend of Noddy in Enid Blyton's children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-Ears is a fictional brownie, a goblin-like sprite in a British children's story.

clue.text: Without dressing, served up as a rule, tuna

indicators.note: served up suggests a dish rearranged on a plate, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: As a rule, tuna is served plain, without any dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Au naturel is French for in its natural state: cooked plainly or, of a person, naked.

clue.text: American poet and essayist's first sermon in new compilation

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the essayist
a new compilation puts the letters together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An American poet and essayist's debut sermon appears in a new anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American poet and essayist' looks like one definition, but 'essayist's first' gives E; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century US writer of verse and essays.

clue.text: Also enthralling doctor, the French kind of lottery

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: also means too
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A French doctor is also captivated by some sort of lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle-style draw where tickets are pulled from a revolving drum, so a type of lottery.

clue.text: Site map clue must be solved to show buried receptacle?

indicators.note: solved here means worked out like a puzzle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clue on a site map must be cracked to find a buried treasure chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A time capsule is a container of items sealed and often buried for people in the future to open.

clue.text: Shorts with English tonic

parts.note: shorts are small measures of spirits, such as gins

explanation.surface: Short drinks served with English tonic water, a bar order.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorts and tonic suggest a gin and tonic; in fact the tonic is the definition, a herbal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a root taken as a restorative remedy, and a restorative is called a tonic.

clue.text: Railway staff in Germany supported by article there to rig vote

indicators.note: in a down answer, supported by means the next piece sits below

parts.note: to staff something is to man it
der is a German definite article, the word for the used in Germany

explanation.surface: Rail workers in Germany are backed by a newspaper article about fixing an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article there' means a word for the in Germany's language: DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To gerrymander is to redraw electoral boundaries for partisan advantage, a way of fixing an election.

clue.text: Individual tucked into my bread

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: taken as written
an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: Someone is eating my loaf, tucking into my bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating but is the container signal. Bread is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is long-standing slang for cash, just as dough is.

clue.text: One who reprimands hunter grabbing its back

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the hunter's word holds another inside

parts.note: a hunter is one who chases, a chaser

indicators.note: back means the word its is read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter scolds the animal after grabbing it by its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as the animal's body but is the reversal signal; the turned word sits after the hunter's third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to rebuke or scold, so someone who chastises is a scolder.

clue.text: Friendly drink

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit-flavoured concentrate diluted with water

explanation.surface: A friendly drink, offered with a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warmly sociable as an adjective, and as a noun it is a fruit syrup drink.

clue.text: Printer a liability? To some extent, among other things

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is a printer a liability? Partly, among other things, an office gripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' says the letters lie within 'Printer a liability', spanning all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is a Latin phrase used in English meaning including others besides.

clue.text: Agent taking in band that's bouncy

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an agent is a secret operative, a spy
a band is a ring, as a wedding band

explanation.surface: A secret agent takes in a band that is lively and bouncy.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy describes something elastic that rebounds, which is the sense of bouncy.

clue.text: Cockney's feet getting to grips with one system of exercises

indicators.note: getting to grips with means grasping, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang feet are plates of meat, shortened to plates
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Londoner's feet are grappling with one form of exercise regime.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is a London dialect where a word is replaced by a rhyming phrase, often shortened: plates of meat for feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a regime of controlled movements for core strength, named after its inventor.

clue.text: Insects found in place across street

indicators.note: across means spread over, so the place word straddles the street

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

explanation.surface: Bugs are discovered somewhere on the far side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are swarming grasshoppers, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Examined son, drunk

parts.note: canned is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A doctor checked over a son who was intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanned means looked over carefully or inspected, a synonym of examined.

clue.text: Bachelor girl in Spanish-speaking country

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman living in a Spanish-speaking land.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a South American republic where Spanish is an official language.

clue.text: Jonson, perhaps — electronic image good

parts.note: Ben Jonson was an English playwright, so Ben is an example name
an E-fit is a computer-built picture of a suspect's face used by police

explanation.surface: Ben Jonson, perhaps, makes a fine figure in an electronic portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' looks like a description of the image; it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage, something done for one's good or welfare.

clue.text: Leave Virginia with American beast

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
the moose is a large deer of North America

explanation.surface: Escape Virginia along with a big American animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is informal American slang meaning go away quickly or scram.

clue.text: A nice turn in variety? Not sure

indicators.note: in variety means in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is that a pleasing act in a variety show? Not sure.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a music-hall act, which makes 'variety' look like a theatre show; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain means doubtful or unconvinced, which is what not sure says.

clue.text: Not very bright Italian, retiring, shy

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: dim means not clever, or not shining
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A dull-witted Italian who is retiring and shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like part of the definition next to shy, but it reverses both preceding pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid means lacking confidence or easily frightened, the same as shy.

clue.text: What a pope may wear in a short ceremony round area to the north

indicators.note: in a down answer, going to the north means the letters read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the ceremony word encloses the area letter
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: The headgear a pontiff might wear during a brief ritual in the vicinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts RITE to RIT; 'round' puts A inside to make RAIT; A plus RAIT is turned by 'to the north', reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal tiara is a triple crown worn by popes on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Piles showered on Greek character

indicators.note: showered suggests scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Piles of something are rained down on a Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: Character here is a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a written symbol in Greek.

clue.text: Character left wearing support

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the support word goes round the other letter

parts.note: to support someone is to favour them

explanation.surface: A character on the left wearing some kind of brace.
explanation.definitionFit: Flavour can mean the distinctive quality or tone of something, its character.

clue.text: Pay for a guy in order to relax

parts.note: to stand a round is to pay for it
to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: Treat a man to something so that he can unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb meaning ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand at ease is the military command to relax one's posture, hence an idiom for loosening up.
